title: Lemma A(iii): lower semicontinuity of Phi_n and limiting reduction to simple roots

comments.author: human
comments.body:
The reduction to the simple-root case uses the smoothing operator $T_\epsilon=(1-\epsilon\,d/dx)^n$ and requires a delicate limit $\epsilon\to0$.

**Key subtlety:** $\Phi_n$ is NOT continuous at multiple roots; it blows up to $+\infty$. The correct property is *lower semicontinuity* of $\Phi_n$ on $\mathbb R^n$ (extended-real valued), equivalently *upper semicontinuity* of $1/\Phi_n$.

**Required to prove:**
1. $\Phi_n$ is lower semicontinuous: on the open simple-root locus it is continuous; near any coalescence of roots at least one score $\to\pm\infty$, forcing $\Phi_n\to+\infty$.
2. $1/\Phi_n(T_\epsilon p)\to 1/\Phi_n(p)$ and $1/\Phi_n(T_\epsilon^2(p\boxplus_n q))\to 1/\Phi_n(p\boxplus_n q)$ as $\epsilon\to0$, **including the case where $p$ (or $q$) already has multiple roots** (then the corresponding RHS term is $0$ and only $\limsup$ control is needed).
3. Inequality direction: from $(\star)$ for $(T_\epsilon p,T_\epsilon q)$, pass to the limit taking $\limsup$ on the LHS (USC) and $\lim$ on the RHS.

**Verified numerically:** $T_\epsilon$ preserves real-rootedness and separates multiple roots into simple ones for $\epsilon>0$.

comments.author: solver-agent
comments.body:
**Resolution — issue verified as substantively addressed; one clarifying addition made.**

I reviewed the relevant section of `solution.tex` (Lemma `lem:simple` = "Lemma A(iii)", the gap-blowup Lemma `lem:gapblowup`, Lemma `lem:Bconv`, and Steps A–C of the reduction). All three required items are present and correct; I verified the underlying claims numerically and added an explicit USC reformulation for transparency.

**Item 1 — LSC of $\Phi_n$ (= USC of $1/\Phi_n$).**
- On the open simple-root locus $U=\{\xi_i\ne\xi_j\}$, $\Phi_n=\|\mathsf S\|^2$ is continuous (Lemma `lem:simple`(ii), Case 1).
- Near a coalescence, Lemma `lem:gapblowup` gives the *correct* (and nontrivial) blow-up: rather than the invalid single-term bound (scores are sums that can cancel), it uses an $\ell^2$ cluster-scaling argument: for a size-$m$ cluster of diameter $d_k\to0$, $\Phi_n\ge \rho_m/(2d_k^2)-O(1)$ with $\rho_m=\inf_{K_m'}\Phi_n\ge1>0$. I numerically confirmed $\rho_2=2,\ \rho_3=18,\ \rho_4\approx65$ (all $>0$, so $\rho_m\ge1$ is a safe sufficient bound).
- I **added** an explicit paragraph proving the equivalence "LSC of $\Phi_n$ $\Leftrightarrow$ USC of $1/\Phi_n$" via the decreasing homeomorphism $t\mapsto1/t$ of $(0,\infty]\to[0,\infty)$, since USC of $1/\Phi_n$ is the form actually used in Step C. This directly answers the issue's "equivalently upper semicontinuity of $1/\Phi_n$".

**Item 2 — $1/\Phi_n(T_\epsilon p)\to1/\Phi_n(p)$ including the multiple-root case.**
Lemma `lem:Bconv` splits into Case 1 (simple roots: full continuity) and Case 2 ($p$ has a root of multiplicity $m\ge2$: then RHS term $1/\Phi_n(p)=0$, and $\Phi_n(T_\epsilon p)\ge\rho_m/(2d_\epsilon^2)-mC^2\to+\infty$, using only $d_\epsilon\to0$, not the rate). This is exactly the "only $\limsup$ control needed; RHS term is $0$" point. The same applies to $T_\epsilon^2(p\boxplus_n q)$ via Step C. Numerically verified: for $p=(x-1)^2(x+2)$ (double root), $1/\Phi_n(p)=0$, and along the Nuij family $b_\epsilon\to L=1/\Phi_n(q)$ while $a_\epsilon\to1/\Phi_n(p\boxplus q)$.

**Item 3 — Inequality direction (limit passage).**
From $(\star)$ for $(T_\epsilon p,T_\epsilon q)$, i.e. $a_\epsilon\ge b_\epsilon$:
- RHS: $b_\epsilon\to L=1/\Phi_n(p)+1/\Phi_n(q)$ (Item 2, true limit).
- LHS: USC gives $\limsup_\epsilon a_\epsilon\le 1/\Phi_n(p\boxplus q)$ from $\liminf_\epsilon\Phi_n(\cdots)\ge\Phi_n(p\boxplus q)$ (handled including $\Phi_n(p\boxplus q)=\infty$, where it reads $\le0$).
- Chain: $1/\Phi_n(p\boxplus q)\ge\limsup a_\epsilon\ge\liminf a_\epsilon\ge L$.
I numerically confirmed the full passage on a double-root example: $a_\epsilon\to1.5604=1/\Phi_n(p\boxplus q)\ge L=0.7497$, with $a_\epsilon\ge b_\epsilon$ at every $\epsilon$.

**Supporting facts verified numerically:** (a) Nuij separation — $T_\epsilon$ keeps real-rootedness and splits the double root (e.g. root $1$ of multiplicity 2 splits into $\approx1.013,1.047$ at $\epsilon=0.01$); (b) the operator identity $(T_\epsilon p)\boxplus_n(T_\epsilon q)=T_\epsilon^2(p\boxplus_n q)$ to machine precision (Lemma `lem:simple`(iii)).

**Edit made:** inserted a paragraph after the LSC proof in Lemma `lem:simple`(ii) making the LSC$\Leftrightarrow$USC equivalence explicit and tying it to Step C. Dollar/brace balance checked; no LaTeX toolchain available to compile, but the insertion is self-contained inline text.

Conclusion: the gap described in the issue is closed. Marking resolved.
